messages:
Ana (marketing): Quick preflight ask for the Thurs webinar — can runtime run a small prioritized bench for the launch post and live demo? Need coldstart vs warmup, and tail-case numbers (p99/p999). Minimal scope: 3 model variants, ~80 prompts, short + long responses. Ping @Mike (eng-runtime) for feasibility.

Mike (eng-runtime): Can do but need exact payloads + model names + what you mean by 'coldstart' (first request after a long idle, or after a deploy?). Also: do you want network-to-client end-to-end latency or just server-side infer time?

Ana (marketing): Good q — coldstart = first-inference after a 30+ minute idle (we want demo coldstart story). Please measure: 1) pure server-side model latency, 2) end-to-end (client->api->response). We'll provide sample payloads. Model variants: hosted baseline (redwood/7b-standard), quantized low-cost (redwood/7b-q4f16), and an 8-bit aggressive (community/7b-8bit). Keep runs small: 80 prompts x 3 repeats. Warmup protocol: 10 warmup calls (same prompt) then record next 3 as warm steady. Coldstart: single run after 30m idle.

Mike (eng-runtime): Got it. Two clarifications: a) do you need token-level logs (kv/cache hits, batching events)? b) should we include a forced cache-priming scenario (prefix caching) or strictly fresh cache?

Ana (marketing): a) yes, include token-level traces for 5 representative prompts (for the appendix). b) Strictly fresh cache for coldstart measurements; we also want a separate primed-cache run so marketing can show the improvement.

Sam (eng-runtime): FYI on scheduling: medium priority. We can spin up the dedicated quantized variant but might take provisioning ~30m. Estimate full sweep ~90–120 minutes including traces.

Lina (data-science): Add these metrics to the ask: p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 latency (ms), tokens/sec, median and 95% tail for tokens/sec, failure rate, CPU/GPU utilization samples, and rough cost estimate per 1M tokens for each variant. Also request raw trace files (jsonl) for two runs.

Ana (marketing): Copy — we'll own the narrative packaging. Sample payloads (please use these exact JSON shapes):

```json
{
  "id": "short-001",
  "input": "Write a 2-sentence blurb about Redwood Inference focusing on low-latency serving for developers.",
  "max_tokens": 40
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "long-001",
  "input": "Draft a 400-token blog section explaining how prefix caching + batching reduces token costs and an example latency tradeoff.",
  "max_tokens": 512
}
```

Mike (eng-runtime): Perfect — also include the seed if determinism matters. Are we okay with nondeterministic sampling for these?

Ana (marketing): Sampling is fine — we mostly care about timing, not exact text parity. Seed optional.

Mike (eng-runtime): Cool. I'll schedule a canary tonight (low-traffic window) for the quantized variant and a full sweep tomorrow AM. I'll attach run IDs here when kicking off. Expect artifacts: per-request latencies, aggregated percentiles, raw jsonl traces, warmup/coldstart heatmaps.

runtime-bot: Run scheduled by Mike (eng-runtime) — canary job id run-1824683600 queued.

Josh (marketing): Awesome — can you also capture one short video screencap of the live latency dashboard for the demo? 30s clip showing coldstart then warmup.

Sam (eng-runtime): Yep, we'll capture a grafana gif and attach.

Lina (data-science): Reminder: redact any customer PII. Marketing, please confirm none of these prompts contain customer-owned data.

Ana (marketing): Confirmed — prompts are synthetic. Thanks all — we'll wait for the run artifacts and the runbot notifications. :rocket:
